Clean institution names by OpenAlex institution ID

Source: R/institutions_clean.R
institutions_clean.Rd

Gives each institution one name and keeps different institutions apart, using OpenAlex institution IDs (with their ROR IDs where OpenAlex has them). For every paper with a DOI, OpenAlex says which institutions its authors belong to. Papers OpenAlex does not cover, or authors it gives only an address for, are resolved from the address text:

  1. an address OpenAlex has already linked to an institution on another paper gets that institution (`source = "openalex address"`);

  2. otherwise the institution part of the address is taken (the part naming a university, college, academy or hospital, else an institute, centre, lab or company, else the first part), and if OpenAlex knows that name, the institution behind it (`"openalex name"`);

  3. otherwise that part is kept as written (`"address"`).

Two institutions OpenAlex keeps apart that share a name get their country code: `NORTHEASTERN UNIVERSITY`, `NORTHEASTERN UNIVERSITY, CN`. The names from step 3 are the ones left to [suggest_merges()], which never pairs two institutions OpenAlex has identified.

Usage

institutions_clean(
  data,
  affiliations = "C1",
  doi = "DI",
  openalex = TRUE,
  replace = NULL,
  mailto = NULL
)

Arguments

data

Your papers, one row each (a bibliometrix data frame). The result of another `clean_*()` function works too, so the cleaners chain: `M |> authors_clean(scopus = "Dlds") |> keywords_clean()`.

affiliations

The column of author addresses, `;`-separated. Default `"C1"`.

doi

The DOI column. Default `"DI"`.

openalex

Ask OpenAlex (`TRUE`, the default)? With `FALSE` every institution comes from the address text.

replace

Reviewed merges to apply: an [ask_ai()] result, a review sheet from [review_sheet()], or `OLD`/`NEW` tables, as in [keywords_clean()].

mailto

An e-mail address for OpenAlex's polite pool (faster, more reliable). Sent only to OpenAlex, and only when you give it.

Value

A `saqr_institutions` object. Print it for an overview. `as.data.frame(x)` gives your data with `AU_UN` (each paper's institutions, `;`-separated, in author order) and `AU_UN_ID` (their OpenAlex IDs, `NA` where none). `what = "institutions"`: one row per institution: `institution`, `openalex_id`, `ror`, `country`, `type`, `papers`, `source`. [institutions_changes()]: one row per paper and institution: `paper`, `address` (the text it came from; empty when OpenAlex named it directly), `institution`, `openalex_id`, `source`. `summary()` counts papers and institutions per `source`; names renamed by `replace` have `source = "review"`. A review never renames an institution OpenAlex identified: a name from address text renamed to an identified institution's name joins it, ID and all.

Errors

Raises `saqrmisc_bad_input` for a missing or non-character column, or a bad `openalex` or `mailto`; `saqrmisc_missing_package` when `openalex = TRUE` without httr2. Failed OpenAlex requests warn `saqrmisc_openalex_failed`; those papers fall back to their addresses.

References

Priem, J., Piwowar, H., & Orr, R. (2022). OpenAlex: A fully-open index of scholarly works, authors, venues, institutions, and concepts. *arXiv*. doi:10.48550/arXiv.2205.01833

See also

[suggest_merges()], [authors_clean()], [keywords_clean()]

Examples

papers <- data.frame(
  DI = NA_character_,
  C1 = c("DEPARTMENT OF COMPUTING, UNIVERSITY OF TURKU, TURKU, FINLAND",
         "SCHOOL OF EDUCATION, UNIVERSITY OF EASTERN FINLAND, JOENSUU, FINLAND")
)
institutions <- institutions_clean(papers, openalex = FALSE)
institutions
#> Institutions by OpenAlex ID (OpenAlex not asked)
#>   2 institutions in 2 of 2 papers: 0 identified by OpenAlex, 2 from address text only
#>   links: openalex 0, openalex address 0, openalex name 0, review 0, address 2
#> as.data.frame(x) gives the cleaned papers; institutions_changes(x) what each address became.
#> suggest_merges(x) proposes merges among the names OpenAlex did not identify.
